energy_accounting.study_energy_disclosure: Public financial filings and task cost equations; no new hardware meter attached.

claims.statement: Open methods routinely run AI far more cheaply on existing machines, yet products often wait months or years to adopt them.
Machine hardware costs far more per task than raw electricity, backed by both operating cash and circular supplier investments.
Corporate calendars delay rollouts in quarterly steps until automation tools slash switching friction and force cheaper methods into production.
Headline outcome: Electricity < 12% of Task Cost · Switching Is the Moat (Public financial filings and task cost equations; no new hardware meter attached.)

easy_read.easy_title: Why Cheaper Open AI Takes Months to Ship
three_points_one_idea_sentences: This study is about why cheaper open ai takes months to ship.
Open methods routinely run AI far more cheaply on existing machines, yet products often wait months or years to adopt them.
Machine hardware costs far more per task than raw electricity, backed by both operating cash and circular supplier investments.
Corporate calendars delay rollouts in quarterly steps until automation tools slash switching friction and force cheaper methods into production.
Key result: Electricity < 12% of Task Cost · Switching Is the Moat.
Clear math and public price records checked every number.
